classification.difficultyReason: Translate each depression angle into a right triangle and use tangent to find horizontal distance. The parts explicitly scaffold the remaining routine links: subtract the distances and divide by five seconds.

content.prompt: A police helicopter, hovering at an altitude of $1000\text{ m}$, observes a car travelling along a straight highway. At that instant, the angle of depression of the car from the helicopter is $27^{\circ}$. Five seconds later, the angle of depression of the car from the helicopter is $26^{\circ}$. The highway is level and passes through the point directly below the helicopter. The car travels away from that point throughout the $5$ seconds.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the horizontal distance the car is from the helicopter when it is first sighted, giving your answer correct to the nearest tenth of a metre?

answer.worked:
Let $x_1$ metres be the initial horizontal distance. The angle of elevation from the car equals the angle of depression, by alternate angles between parallel horizontals.
$$\begin{align*}\tan27^{\circ}&=\frac{1000}{x_1}\\x_1\tan27^{\circ}&=1000\\x_1&=\frac{1000}{\tan27^{\circ}}\\x_1&\approx1962.6\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the horizontal distance the car is from the helicopter $5$ seconds after it is first sighted, giving your answer correct to the nearest tenth of a metre.

answer.worked:
Let $x_2$ metres be the horizontal distance after $5$ seconds. The angle of elevation is $26^{\circ}$, by alternate angles.
$$\begin{align*}\tan26^{\circ}&=\frac{1000}{x_2}\\x_2\tan26^{\circ}&=1000\\x_2&=\frac{1000}{\tan26^{\circ}}\\x_2&\approx2050.3\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the distance the car has travelled in the $5$ seconds, giving your answer correct to the nearest tenth of a metre.

answer.short:
$87.7\text{ m}$

Subtract the unrounded horizontal distances.
answer.worked:
The car travels away along the level highway, so its distance travelled is the difference between the horizontal distances. Retain the unrounded values.
$$\begin{align*}s&=x_2-x_1\\s&=\frac{1000}{\tan26^{\circ}}-\frac{1000}{\tan27^{\circ}}\\s&\approx87.7\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: What is the speed at which the car is travelling in metres per second, correct to $1$ decimal place?

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded distance from part c. The speed over the interval is distance divided by time.
$$\begin{align*}v&=\frac{s}{5}\\v&=\frac{1000/\tan26^{\circ}-1000/\tan27^{\circ}}{5}\\v&\approx17.5\text{ m/s}\end{align*}$$
